items.title: DeepMind agents find faster quantum algorithms, each result proved in Lean
items.what_happened: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve known quantum algorithms. Every result is checked in Lean. Claimed gains include an 11.8x cheaper fusion-relevant circuit and a 2.5x better cytochrome P450 simulation.
items.why_it_matters: It pairs open-ended agent search with formal proofs, so claims can be checked by a machine. The Lean library, problem specs and verified solutions are open source.
items.what_to_watch: Whether outside groups use the open library to verify or extend the results, and whether the method carries over to classical algorithm search.
items.research_area: AI agents, AI for science, formal verification
items.uncertainty: The authors say the algorithms still need more resources than early error-corrected machines will likely have.

items.title: ShellBench: top agents fail everyday personal tasks over a third of the time
items.what_happened: ShellBench tests personal agents on everyday tasks drawn from over 10 million anonymised real agent interactions. Top models failed more than a third of the time, and 15.7% of attempts broke at least one safety rule.
items.why_it_matters: It measures safety and correctness together on realistic tasks. About 10% of otherwise correct runs still broke a safety rule, a gap that plain success rates hide.
items.what_to_watch: A paper or code release, and whether results hold in each product's own harness, which were not all tested.
items.uncertainty: Reported through a news article. The original post was not opened and no repository is linked.

items.title: Thinking Machines opens a looped MoE model, and Goodfire publishes a first look inside
items.what_happened: Inkling 2 Mini is an open-weights Mixture-of-Experts model under Apache 2.0. Its two middle blocks run three times, so 24 layers give 48 layer passes per token. Goodfire had early access and mapped how information flows through the loops.
items.why_it_matters: Looped, weight-shared depth is a different route to efficiency than a bigger model. Open weights let researchers test whether looping helps reasoning and how standard interpretability tools cope.
items.what_to_watch: Independent evaluations against similar-size models, and whether logit-lens style tools need changes for looped models.
items.uncertainty: Benchmarks are company reported. Goodfire calls its findings early results.

notes: Covered via lab blogs (Anthropic Alignment, DeepMind, Goodfire) and web search. The Anthropic neuron-basis posts were already covered yesterday. X and LinkedIn not used.
